Topics · The prophets

Why do Sikhs and the Quran both say God is One?

The Mool Mantar and the Quran begin with the One, unborn. What does it mean when two roads start at one point?

Part 1 of 3

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ١ ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ٢﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "He is Allāh, [who is] One,[2011] Allāh, the Eternal Refuge.[2012]

Translator's notes

[2011] Alone, without another, indivisible with absolute and permanent unity and distinct from all else. The one and only true deity, unique in His essence, attributes and deeds.

[2012] He who is absolute, perfect, complete, essential, self-sufficient and sufficient to meet the needs of all creation; the one eternally and constantly required and sought, depended upon by all existence and to whom all matters will ultimately return.

Quran · Al-Ikhlas 112:1-2

Translation

Yahweh will be King over all the earth. In that day Yahweh will be one, and his name one.

Original · Hebrew

וְהָיָ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִהְיֶ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶחָ֖ד וּשְׁמ֥וֹ אֶחָֽד׃

Zechariah · 14:9

World English Bible

Two children from two distant villages meet at a river. They speak in different dialects and discover that their grandmothers sing the same tune. The families never met. The children cannot say how the tune travelled, but they know it is one. So the song is a question before it is an answer.

A question for you

When two texts agree to begin with the One, which of these questions comes first for you?

If you sayHow did each come to know it?
ThenA good question. The verses ahead look at the road of reasoning: what is left standing when we think?
If you sayIs it really the same thing?
ThenAn honest question. The answer is not complete here. What is shared is the starting point; what comes after deserves a careful reading.
If you sayWhat does it mean to start from one place?
ThenThat is the question this page asks in its title, and you will answer it in your own words at the end.

Part 2 of 3

﴿أَمْ خُلِقُوا۟ مِنْ غَيْرِ شَىْءٍ أَمْ هُمُ ٱلْخَـٰلِقُونَ٣٥ أَمْ خَلَقُوا۟ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ ۚ بَل لَّا يُوقِنُونَ٣٦﴾

Translation of the meaning

Or were they created by nothing, or were they the creators [of themselves]? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain.

Quran · At-Tur 52:35-36

Translation

I beg you, my child, to lift your eyes to the sky and the earth, and to see all things that are in it, and thus to recognize that God made them not of things that were, and that the race of men in this way comes into being.

Original · Ancient Greek

Ἀξιῶ σε, τέκνον, ἀναβλέψαντα εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς πάντα ἰδόντα, γνῶναι ὅτι ἐξ οὐκ ὄντων ἐποίησεν αὐτὰ ὁ Θεὸς, καὶ τὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένος οὕτως γεγένηται,

2 Maccabees · 7:28

World English Bible

A man finds a basket of fresh bread at his door every morning. He asks his neighbours, and they all deny it. He stays up to see who comes. It never crossed his mind that it could have no giver. His question is the verse's: from nothing? Did he make it himself? Or another maker?

A question for you

Which of the three can you honestly hold about yourself?

If you sayI came from nothing
ThenThat would mean nothing produced bone, blood and a mind that asks questions. Can you hold that? The answer is yours.
If you sayI made myself
ThenThat would mean you were there before you were. The verse asks whether that is possible.
If you saySomeone other than me made me
ThenThat enters the third door the verse leaves to the reader. It meets the word “Creator” at the start of the Mool Mantar.

Part 3 of 3

﴿لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ٣ وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌۢ٤﴾

Translation of the meaning

He neither begets nor is born, Nor is there to Him any equivalent."

Quran · Al-Ikhlas 112:3-4

Translation

To whom then will you liken God? Or what likeness will you compare to him? “To whom then will you liken me? Who is my equal?” says the Holy One.

Original · Hebrew

וְאֶל־מִ֖י תְּדַמְּי֣וּן אֵ֑ל וּמַה־דְּמ֖וּת תַּ֥עַרְכוּ לֽוֹ׃ וְאֶל־מִ֥י תְדַמְּי֖וּנִי וְאֶשְׁוֶ֑ה יֹאמַ֖ר קָדֽוֹשׁ׃

Isaiah · 40:18, 25

World English Bible

At the source of a river a boy asks his grandfather where the water comes from. The mountain, says the old man. And the mountain? The grandfather laughs and says, ask the mountain. Every “from where” leads to what came before, until we reach what has no before. There the question stops, and the chapter stops.

A question for you

What has to be true of the first source for the chain to stop there?

If you sayThat it has no beginning
ThenThat is what the Mool Mantar names and what the chapter says. One question remains: what marks out what has no beginning?
If you sayThat it needs nothing
ThenThat is the quality of as-Samad, in the second line of the chapter. What needs nothing is not propped on another.
If you sayThat nothing is like it
ThenThat is how the chapter closes. If nothing is like it, nothing can measure it, and no picture of it can be drawn.

The same in the other books
